```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)

here::i_am("errata.qmd")

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

out <- function(file) {
  read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", file), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

one_dp <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
two_dp <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)

# Entry 1: the two study rows of table 2.2, whose labels are interchanged.
table_2.2 <- out("table_2.2_lrl_reanalysis.csv")
lrl_cell <- function(content_label, panel, group) {
  row <- table_2.2 |>
    filter(content_factor == content_label, outcome_variable == panel)
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  one_dp(row[[paste("Capital Punishment", group)]])
}
pro_study <- function(panel, group) lrl_cell("After pro capital punishment study", panel, group)
anti_study <- function(panel, group) lrl_cell("After anti capital punishment study", panel, group)

# Entry 2: the Hiscox expert cue persistence estimates.
table_6.4 <- out("table_6.4_all_persistence.csv")
hiscox <- function(sample_label) {
  row <- table_6.4 |>
    filter(str_starts(study_label, "Hiscox"), Sample == sample_label,
           Treatment == "Expert cue")
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  100 * as.numeric(str_extract(row$`Persistence Ratio`, "^[-0-9.]+"))
}
hiscox_mturk <- round(hiscox("MTurk"))
hiscox_gfk <- round(hiscox("GfK"))

# Entry 3: the convincingness ratings in the lower half of table 2.3.
convincing <-
  out("table_2.3_gc_replication.csv") |>
  filter(rating == "convincing", str_detect(predisposition, "Proponents"))
stopifnot(nrow(convincing) == 1)

# Entry 4: the standard error of the two-sided effect on support among opponents.
two_sided_se <-
  out("figure_5.17_gc_pro_con_effects.csv") |>
  filter(dv == "support_recode_change", term == "Pro Con",
         predisposition == "Capital Punishment Opponents")
stopifnot(nrow(two_sided_se) == 1)
```

Four errata in *Persuasion in Parallel: How Information Changes Minds about Politics*
(University of Chicago Press, 2022), <https://doi.org/10.7208/chicago/9780226821832.001.0001>.
None of the four changes any conclusion the book draws. Every corrected value below is
computed at render time from the maintained reanalysis in `active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2022`.

**Provenance.** Each correction below was checked against the printed edition. The
reanalysis itself reads an uncorrected proof dated 26 May 2022, so the quoted wording was
verified against the published book rather than taken from that file, and the four
discrepancies are properties of the analysis rather than of any one rendering.

---

**1.** In table 2.2 (p. 26), the two study rows carry each other's labels, in both panels.

> Change in attitudes toward the death penalty
>
> | | Proponents | Opponents |
> |---|---|---|
> | After **pro**-capital punishment study | `r anti_study("attitude", "Proponents")` | `r anti_study("attitude", "Opponents")` |
> | After **anti**-capital punishment study | `r pro_study("attitude", "Proponents")` | `r pro_study("attitude", "Opponents")` |
>
> Change in beliefs in deterrent efficacy
>
> | | Proponents | Opponents |
> |---|---|---|
> | After **pro**-capital punishment study | `r anti_study("belief", "Proponents")` | `r anti_study("belief", "Opponents")` |
> | After **anti**-capital punishment study | `r pro_study("belief", "Proponents")` | `r pro_study("belief", "Opponents")` |

*Corrected:*

> Change in attitudes toward the death penalty
>
> | | Proponents | Opponents |
> |---|---|---|
> | After **anti**-capital punishment study | `r anti_study("attitude", "Proponents")` | `r anti_study("attitude", "Opponents")` |
> | After **pro**-capital punishment study | `r pro_study("attitude", "Proponents")` | `r pro_study("attitude", "Opponents")` |
>
> Change in beliefs in deterrent efficacy
>
> | | Proponents | Opponents |
> |---|---|---|
> | After **anti**-capital punishment study | `r anti_study("belief", "Proponents")` | `r anti_study("belief", "Opponents")` |
> | After **pro**-capital punishment study | `r pro_study("belief", "Proponents")` | `r pro_study("belief", "Opponents")` |

The changed artifact is the two labels alone. Every value is correct, and the rows are in
the order the analysis produces them, whose study-content factor runs con before pro and so
puts the anti-capital punishment study first. Figure 2.2, printed on the same page from the
same variable, shows the con study at `r anti_study("attitude", "Proponents")` for
proponents and `r anti_study("attitude", "Opponents")` for opponents and the pro study at
`r pro_study("attitude", "Proponents")` and `r pro_study("attitude", "Opponents")`, which is
the table's two rows the other way up. The sentence beneath the figure, reporting that
self-assessed change is higher in the pro condition than in the null and higher in the null
than in the con, says the same thing again. The "Combined" rows are sums of the two and are
unaffected, as is the reading of the table that the surrounding text draws from them.

---

**2.** Page 114 attributes a persistence estimate to a sample that is not in the
persistence analysis.

> Curiously, the different replications of the Hiscox (2006) "expert" treatment generated
> very different persistence estimates: `r hiscox_mturk` percent on MTurk but
> `r hiscox_gfk` percent on **Lucid**.

*Corrected:*

> Curiously, the different replications of the Hiscox (2006) "expert" treatment generated
> very different persistence estimates: `r hiscox_mturk` percent on MTurk but
> `r hiscox_gfk` percent on **GfK**.

Table 6.1 lists twelve panel survey experiments and none of them is fielded on Lucid; the
Hiscox rows of table 6.4 are Mechanical Turk and GfK, and table 6.4 gives the zero to GfK.
The two percentages are left at the whole numbers the sentence uses because they come from
a bootstrap the analysis runs without a seed, and a decimal place would state a precision
the estimator does not have.

---

**3.** In the lower half of table 2.3, the difference between the two convincingness
ratings for proponents does not equal the difference between the two cells printed above
it.

The table prints `r one_dp(convincing$pro_study)` for the pro-capital punishment study and
`r one_dp(convincing$anti_study)` for the anti-capital punishment study, and gives their
difference as **3.0**. The difference is **`r one_dp(convincing$difference)`**. The changed
artifact is that single cell; every other cell in both halves of the table reproduces.

---

**4.** Page 101 gives a standard error that disagrees with the book's own appendix
table A.5.

> As shown in the left facet, the average effect of the two-sided message on support for
> capital punishment is very close to zero for both proponents (0.28 scale points, SE:
> 0.18) and opponents (0.10, SE: **0.11**).

*Corrected:*

> As shown in the left facet, the average effect of the two-sided message on support for
> capital punishment is very close to zero for both proponents (0.28 scale points, SE:
> 0.18) and opponents (0.10, SE: **`r two_dp(two_sided_se$std.error)`**).

Table A.5 reports `r two_dp(two_sided_se$std.error)` for this same standard error, and the
reanalysis reproduces the appendix. The other seven quantities in the passage are correct
as printed.
